sources.name: OpenStreetMap seamarks
sources.notes: Worldwide, queryable AtoN via the Overpass API. Coverage is densest in Europe and the US; some regions map no bifurcation or range marks at all.

sources.name: NOAA ENC Direct to GIS
sources.licence: CC0 1.0 (NOAA Coast Survey data; verify third-party feature provenance)
sources.notes: One chart-feature wreck in the New York Harbor query bounds, retained as a separate source feature. NOAA states ENC Direct to GIS is not certified for navigation; use current official ENCs for navigation. Retrieval snapshot: data-raw/noaa-ny-harbor-wrecks.geojson.

sources.name: EMODnet Human Activities — Heritage Shipwrecks
sources.notes: Solent heritage inventory snapshot with Historic England source attribution. The layer includes Polygon centroid points and heterogeneous, historical depth information; not navigation-grade. Only HMS/m A1 and HMS Invincible records were matched to OSM chart marks within 25 m. Retrieval snapshot: data-raw/emodnet-solent-heritage-wrecks.geojson.

sources.name: OpenSeaMap
sources.notes: Transparent seamark tile overlay used directly as a Leaflet layer; the marks themselves come from the OSM extract, not from the raster.

sources.name: OpenCPN chart catalogue
sources.notes: Catalogue of free and paid chart sets. Most entries are raster, registration-gated or non-redistributable, so they cannot feed a bundled AtoN database.

sources.name: C-MAP (Navico)
sources.notes: Licensed ENC. No public tile or data endpoint; cannot be redistributed or queried.

sources.name: Marine Charts Worldwide (gpsnauticalcharts.com)
sources.notes: Aggregated raster charts. No open AtoN API.

sources.name: i-Boating
sources.notes: Commercial chart app. No public endpoint.

sources.name: SHOM (France)
sources.licence: Licence Ouverte for some products, otherwise commercial
sources.notes: Some open data, but the AtoN layers are not published as a queryable endpoint.

sources.name: BSH (Germany)
sources.notes: Open German ENC (S-57) downloads. Ingestable in principle, but downloads are large and region-limited, so it is not part of this build.

sources.name: Rijkswaterstaat (Netherlands)
sources.notes: Open Dutch data; Dutch AtoN feeds are partly mirrored into OSM, which is what this build uses.

sources.name: LINZ (New Zealand)
sources.notes: Open NZ hydrographic data; region outside this build.

sources.name: AMSA (Australia)
sources.notes: Australian AtoN data; not an API, region outside this build.

sources.name: Canadian Hydrographic Service
sources.notes: Open Canadian ENC (S-57). Region outside this build; OSM covers the main Canadian ports.

sources.name: Traficom (Finland)
sources.notes: Open Finnish fairway data; region outside this build.
